# Telar — Project Overview

*Generated by the BMad document-project workflow — deep scan, 2026-07-17.*

## Purpose

Telar is a project-centric agentic development tool built on the Claude Agent SDK. Its
thesis, stated verbatim in the root [README.md](../README.md):

> **Generation is solved; verification is the moat.**

The product runs **looms** — self-verifying units of work that plan, fan out into
parallel threads, build, and verify against an explicit contract. The load-bearing
design constraint, confirmed in code (not just docs), is that a loom never accepts its
own work: acceptance from `ready` to `done` is a human action, and there is no
agent-callable `accept` tool anywhere in the codebase. The `packages/core` engine
enforces this by construction (`packages/core/src/looms.ts`, `packages/core/src/tick.ts`)
and `apps/web` enforces it again at the UI/API boundary with a `PreToolUse` hook that
force-routes loom-affecting tool calls through an interactive permission card
(`apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts`) — the moat is structural, not a convention either
layer trusts the other to uphold.

The design law stated in `packages/core` (see [./architecture-core.md](./architecture-core.md))
is: **deterministic control flow in code, intelligence in the leaves**. Every
scheduling/repair/escalation decision (`tick()`, `decide()`, `rollupWeave`,
`decideRepairContinuation`) is a pure function over integers, sets, and injected
clocks; LLM calls are isolated behind schema-forced `agent()` invocations
(zod-validated `emit_result`) with explicit tool allow/deny lists.

## Executive Summary

Telar implements a **loom lifecycle**: `scope → orchestrate → build → verify →
(repair) → ready → human accept → done`. The three architectural roles from the
README map onto real modules:

- **Loom** — a unit of work tracked as filesystem-backed state under `TELAR_HOME`
  (`~/.telar` by default, overridable via the `TELAR_HOME` env var — see
  `packages/core/src/manifest.ts`, `packages/core/src/looms.ts`). Each loom carries
  spec bundles, events, and a git-worktree-isolated working copy
  (`packages/core/src/vcs.ts`, `packages/core/src/build-fanout.ts`).
- **Weaver (orchestrator)** — a deterministic tick loop (`packages/core/src/tick.ts`,
  `packages/core/src/weave.ts`) that decomposes an objective into parallel
  git-worktree-isolated **threads**, schedules them under a budget
  (`packages/core/src/budget.ts`), and folds results back via `rollupWeave`. Threads
  execute through `packages/core/src/executor.ts` (the largest module in core, ~155K).
- **Verifier** — a read-only agent stack (`packages/core/src/verifier.ts`,
  `packages/core/src/verify-thread.ts`, `packages/core/src/verify-lane.ts`,
  `packages/core/src/critic.ts`, `packages/core/src/panel.ts`) that drives the running
  app (via a browser-automation MCP tool) and checks work against a Verification
  Contract (`packages/core/src/weave-contracts.ts`). It is capability-walled — no
  write/edit tools are granted — so a passing verdict cannot be self-issued. A bounded,
  guarded auto-repair loop (`packages/core/src/repair-guard.ts`) is the only path back
  from a red verdict to another build attempt.
- **Human accept** — `ready → done` is a human-only transition. `apps/web`'s
  `/api/chat` route enforces this again at the tool layer with a `PreToolUse` hook that
  forces `start_loom` / `answer_blocked` (and equivalent loom-affecting calls) through
  an interactive permission card regardless of the SDK's configured permission mode.

The **environment lanes** substrate (`packages/core/src/servers.ts`,
`packages/core/src/supervisor.ts`) runs project dev servers under a `servers.yaml`
declaration with a supervisor that restarts on death, giving the verifier a live
target to drive. A from-scratch **MCP OAuth 2.1** client
(`packages/core/src/mcp-oauth.ts`) lets looms authenticate against remote MCP servers
without an external auth library.

| Part | Category | Technology | Version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Monorepo | Package manager / workspaces | Bun workspaces (`apps/*`, `packages/*`) | Bun (see `bunfig.toml`; no pinned version file) |
| core | Language / runtime | TypeScript, ESM (`"type": "module"`) | TypeScript ^6.0.3 |
| core | Agent SDK | `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` | ^0.3.204 |
| core | Serialization | `yaml` | ^2.9.0 |
| core | Schema validation | `zod` | ^4.4.3 |
| core | Test runner | Bun built-in test runner (`bun test`) | via Bun |
| web | Framework | Next.js (App Router, canary) | ^16.3.0-canary.80 |
| web | UI library | React / React DOM | 19.2.4 |
| web | Agent SDK | `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` | ^0.3.204 |
| web | LLM SDK / streaming | Vercel `ai` SDK | ^7.0.17 |
| web | Internal dependency | `@telar/core` | `workspace:*` |
| web | Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 + `@tailwindcss/postcss` | ^4 |
| web | Component system | `shadcn`, `@base-ui/react` | shadcn ^4.13.0, base-ui ^1.6.0 |
| web | Markdown rendering | `streamdown` (+ `@streamdown/cjk`, `code`, `math`, `mermaid` plugins) | ^2.5.0 (plugins ^1.x) |
| web | Icons / motion / misc UI | `lucide-react`, `motion`, `cmdk`, `embla-carousel-react`, `tw-animate-css`, `use-stick-to-bottom` | see `apps/web/package.json` |
| web | Schema validation | `zod` | ^4.4.3 |
| web | Browser automation (verifier tool, dev dep) | `@playwright/mcp`, `@playwright/test` | ^0.0.77 / ^1.61.1 |
| web | Lint | ESLint + `eslint-config-next` | ^9 / 16.2.10 |
| desktop | Shell runtime | Electron | ^43.1.1 |
| desktop | Packaging | electron-builder | ^26.15.3 |
| desktop | Payload | Bundles `apps/web`'s Next.js standalone build + the `apps/engine` daemon bundle + the Agent SDK's JavaScript + `@playwright/mcp` CLI. The SDK's native Claude binary is NOT bundled — the engine runs the user's own install. | n/a |
| tooling | Type checking | TypeScript | web ^5, core ^6.0.3 (not unified) |

Note: TypeScript is **not** version-unified across the monorepo — `apps/web`
pins `^5` while `packages/core` pins `^6.0.3` (verified in each `package.json`).

```
telar/
├── apps/
│   ├── web/            Next.js cockpit (App Router). Imports @telar/core via workspace:*.
│   │   ├── app/         routes, layouts, and app/api/** (56 route.ts files, 70 HTTP handlers)
│   │   ├── lib/          client/server helpers, 9 *.test.ts spec files
│   │   ├── AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md   Next.js-canary agent guidance (@AGENTS.md import)
│   │   └── README.md    stock create-next-app boilerplate (not project-specific)
│   └── desktop/         Electron shell ("viable tier"). No custom menus/tray/IPC/auto-update.
│       ├── main.js, server-preload.js   forks the packaged Next standalone server, opens a BrowserWindow
│       ├── build-web.sh, install-app.sh
│       └── package.json  electron-builder config (extraResources bundles the Next standalone output + the engine bundle + the Agent SDK + playwright-mcp)
├── packages/
│   └── core/             @telar/core — the loom engine (pure TypeScript library, no build step; exports source directly)
│       ├── src/           59 non-test modules: engine.ts, tick.ts, weave.ts, executor.ts, verifier.ts,
│       │                  verify-thread.ts, critic.ts, panel.ts, repair-guard.ts, servers.ts, supervisor.ts,
│       │                  mcp-oauth.ts, manifest.ts, looms.ts, vcs.ts, budget.ts, schemas.ts, ...
│       │                  └── runner/   out-of-process runner transport (http-transport, lease, liveness, recover)
│       │                  └── setup/    setup-agent.ts
│       │                  └── ultra/    parallel-run harness (executor, runner, sandbox, storage, journal)
│       └── test/         98 *.test.ts spec files (bun test)
├── scripts/               repo tooling (not a workspace part)
│   ├── telar              CLI launcher
│   ├── build-desktop.sh   worktree-isolated snapshot → frozen install → standalone build → binary stamping → electron-builder → smoke test → atomic swap
│   ├── backfill-tool-detail.ts
│   └── e2e/
├── docs/                  this generated documentation set
├── telar.yaml             Telar dogfoods itself: adapter "plain", gate `bun test`, empty guardrails
├── bunfig.toml            [test] pathIgnorePatterns skips build-output copies (release/, .next-desktop/)
├── package.json           root workspace manifest (workspaces: apps/*, packages/*), no root build/test scripts
└── README.md              product pitch, model, and layout (verified against code above)
```

## Architecture Classification

- **Overall**: Bun-workspaces monorepo, three parts (`apps/web`, `apps/desktop`,
  `packages/core`) plus non-workspace `scripts/` tooling. No root-level build/test
  script — everything runs per-workspace. No CI/CD pipeline exists in the repo (no
  `.github/workflows` or equivalent found anywhere).
- **core (`packages/core`, `@telar/core`)**: a TypeScript **domain engine library**,
  not a service — no HTTP server of its own, no build step (its `exports` field
  points directly at `./src/index.ts`). Consumed by `apps/web` via `workspace:*`.
  Internally layered as: pure decision functions (tick/weave/gates) → agent-invoking
  orchestration (executor/verifier/critic) → filesystem persistence (manifest/looms
  under `TELAR_HOME`) → process/environment substrate (servers/supervisor) → protocol
  clients (mcp/mcp-oauth). See [./architecture-core.md](./architecture-core.md).
- **web (`apps/web`)**: a **Next.js App Router layered application** — no
  `pages/api`, no `"use server"` server actions anywhere in the tree; all
  server-side surface is `app/api/**/route.ts` (56 files, 70 HTTP method handlers).
  There is **no auth/authz layer** (no `middleware.ts`, no session or API-key checks)
  — this is a local single-user cockpit that trusts its caller by design. The
  centerpiece is `POST /api/chat` (~1,900 lines), a single agent-turn endpoint
  streaming ~17 named SSE event types while running the Claude Agent SDK or a Codex
  app-server bridge. See [./architecture-web.md](./architecture-web.md) and
  [./api-contracts-web.md](./api-contracts-web.md).
- **desktop (`apps/desktop`)**: a minimal **Electron shell** ("viable tier") — no
  custom menus, tray, IPC surface, or auto-update. Its only real complexity is
  environment/bundling glue: it forks the packaged Next.js standalone server (built
  from `apps/web`) as a child process, captures a login-shell `PATH` so CLI tools
  resolve, picks a stable persisted port, and hand-stamps two runtime dependencies
  (`@playwright/mcp` CLI, the Agent SDK's JavaScript) beside the engine bundle and the standalone
  bundle since Next's tracing drops both. A `--smoke` mode boots the real server,
  curls it, and verifies both bundled binaries work — a fail-closed gate used by
  `scripts/build-desktop.sh` after packaging. See
  [./architecture-desktop.md](./architecture-desktop.md).
